name: Clifford phase gadget removal
summary: A phase gadget with phase π/2 can be removed by complementing the connectivity of its targets and adding π/2 to each target.
description:
A phase-free Z-spider $u$ whose only other leg is an X-spider with phase $\frac\pi2$ (in graph-like form: a phase gadget with phase $\frac\pi2$) can be removed: every pair of its neighbours has its connectivity toggled, and $\frac\pi2$ is added to every neighbour. With $-\frac\pi2$ in place of $\frac\pi2$, $-\frac\pi2$ is added instead. In MBQC terms, a vertex measured in the YZ-plane at angle $\pm\frac\pi2$ can be deleted by a local complementation.

As a unitary, a phase gadget on $n$ qubits with phase $\frac\pi2$ is $\exp(-i\frac\pi4 Z\otimes\cdots\otimes Z)$, which (up to global phase) is a CZ gate between every pair of qubits followed by an S gate on each. This is the reason that Clifford phase gadgets never need to remain after simplification. Compare this with the [local complementation simplification](../local-complementation/), which removes a spider with phase $\pm\frac\pi2$ itself.
parameter_notes: n is the number of neighbours of u (shown for n = 3). The neighbours may have any phases and any number of further legs and edges; π/2 is added to their phases and existing edges between them are toggled (the scalar given is for neighbours that are not yet connected).
